Amazon recently hired a Data Engineer for 31 LPA.
Deloitte recently hired a Data Engineer for 20 LPA.
KPMG recently hired a Data Engineer for 23 LPA.

Same pattern.
Same skillset.
Same interview style.

Here are the TOP 12 REAL questions asked across these companies:

𝗦𝗤𝗟

1️⃣ Find employees who earn more than their managers
2️⃣ Identify duplicates in a table
3️⃣ Find 2nd highest salary (multiple ways)
4️⃣ Detect consecutive occurrences in logs

𝗣𝘆𝘁𝗵𝗼𝗻

5️⃣ Reverse a linked list
6️⃣ Check palindrome
7️⃣ Group word frequency
8️⃣ Fibonacci using generators

𝗣𝘆𝗦𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗸

9️⃣ Explain narrow vs wide transformations
🔟 Fix skew in joins
1️⃣1️⃣ Optimize a slow Spark job
1️⃣2️⃣ Implement SCD-2

If you can answer these 12 areas with confidence,
you already have 70–80% of what MNCs test.

Because companies like:-
PwC
EY
Fractal
Tiger Analytics
Citi
CGI
EPAM Systems

don’t hire you for tools.
They hire you for thinking + problem-solving.

𝗞𝗲𝗲𝗽𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝗶𝗻 𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗱, 𝗜 𝗵𝗮𝘃𝗲 𝗽𝗿𝗲𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝗮 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲𝘁𝗲 𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄 𝗣𝗿𝗲𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗚𝘂𝗶𝗱𝗲 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗔𝘇𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗗𝗮𝘁𝗮 𝗘𝗻𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗻𝗲𝗲𝗿𝘀.

Today, I’m sharing an update I never expected to write.

Due to organizational restructuring and change in business requirement, my full-time offer from Oracle Corporation has been revoked.

Over the past several months, I poured my time, energy, and passion into my internship. I learned from exceptional mentors, worked on enterprise systems, challenged myself with unfamiliar technologies, and grew not only as an engineer but also as a person. Like many interns, I believed that this journey would naturally continue into a full-time role.

Unfortunately, some decisions are beyond our control.

While this outcome is disappointing, it does not diminish the value of the experience, the skills I gained, or the relationships I built. I am grateful to my mentors, teammates, and everyone at Oracle who guided and supported me throughout this journey. Their mentorship and encouragement have had a lasting impact on my professional growth.

As a final-year Computer Science student at M.S. Ramaiah Institute of Technology, graduating in 2026, I am actively seeking opportunities in Software Engineering, Backend Development, Full-Stack Development, DevOps, Cloud Computing, CI/CD Automation, Kubernetes-based Infrastructure, Database Management, and other software-focused technology roles.

This is not the ending I had planned, but it is the beginning of a new chapter. I remain committed to learning, building, and contributing wherever I am given the opportunity.

If you know of any suitable openings or can provide a referral, I would sincerely appreciate your support.

Thank you for taking the time to read this.
